stories.title: Bitcoin and Treasury yields fall together as $80,000 recovery fails
stories.summary: Bitcoin and US Treasury yields dropped together on November 3, a rare pairing that usually does not happen. Bitcoin failed to retake $80,000 in the attempt. A separate report projects a $150 billion Treasury cash rebuild that could drain market liquidity into year-end.
stories.whyItMatters: Liquidity tied to Treasury issuance is a key driver of crypto prices, so this rebuild could cap any year-end rally.
whatToWatch: Progress of the projected $150 billion Treasury cash rebuild
Whether bitcoin and yields keep moving together
questions: Why did yields and bitcoin fall together this time?
Will the Treasury cash rebuild proceed as projected?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Treasury yields fall together in rare divergence as $80,000 recovery fails

stories.title: Binance says thinly traded tokens are delaying full replacement of stolen assets
stories.summary: Binance said it has not fully replaced assets stolen in a recent hack. The exchange said some stolen tokens are thinly traded, which makes them hard to source or buy back. Binance gave no timeline for full reimbursement.
stories.whyItMatters: Readers who track exchange security want to know if user funds get made whole, and thin liquidity could stretch out recovery.

sources.title: Binance says thinly traded tokens are delaying full replacement of stolen assets

stories.title: Tether freezes $1.5 billion in 30 minutes after Binance hack, but $729 million escapes
stories.summary: After the Binance hack, Tether froze $1.5 billion in stablecoin assets tied to the stolen funds within 30 minutes. Despite the fast response, about $729 million still escaped the freeze.
stories.whyItMatters: The fast freeze shows stablecoin issuers can act quickly, but the escaped funds show limits on tracing hacked money.
whatToWatch: Whether the remaining $729 million gets frozen or recovered later
Further law enforcement action tied to the hack
questions: Where did the escaped $729 million go?
Will more of the stolen funds get frozen?

stories.title: Hong Kong bank pilot opens 24/7 cash settlement for tokenized fund deals
stories.summary: A bank pilot in Hong Kong now settles cash for tokenized fund transactions around the clock, instead of only during normal banking hours. The pilot is part of a wider push to test tokenized finance infrastructure.
stories.whyItMatters: Round-the-clock settlement is a step toward institutional adoption of tokenized assets, a trend the lane tracks closely.
whatToWatch: Whether the pilot expands to more banks or funds
Any public results or reports from the pilot
questions: Which bank and funds are involved?
How large is the pilot in transaction volume?

stories.title: Bitcoin Lightning fix blocks a probe linking private channels to onchain funding
stories.summary: A fix to Bitcoin's Lightning Network closes a method that let researchers link private payment channels back to the onchain transactions that funded them. The change is meant to restore a privacy gap in Lightning.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning's privacy properties affect bitcoin's fungibility, a technical detail that matters to anyone tracking protocol-level changes.
whatToWatch: Adoption of the fix across Lightning node software
questions: Who built the fix, and how widely is it adopted?
Does the fix fully close the tracing method, or only part of it?

stories.title: Stronger US factory activity complicates Bitcoin's hopes for lower rates
stories.summary: New US factory activity data came in stronger than expected. That reduces the odds of near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts, which crypto markets had been counting on to support prices.
stories.whyItMatters: Rate-cut expectations directly shape risk appetite, so weaker odds of cuts are a headwind for crypto valuations.
whatToWatch: Upcoming Fed meetings and rate decisions
questions: How much do markets now discount a near-term rate cut?

stories.title: Aave borrowers faced up to 36% APR while a freeze blocked fresh collateral
stories.summary: Borrowers on the Aave lending protocol faced interest rates as high as 36% during an incident in which a freeze stopped them from posting fresh collateral. The freeze left some borrowers stuck paying elevated rates.
stories.whyItMatters: A protocol freeze that traps borrowers at high rates raises questions about risk controls at major DeFi lenders.
whatToWatch: Any borrower losses or forced liquidations tied to the incident
questions: How long did the freeze last, and who was affected most?

stories.title: Crypto industry spent $55 million defending a senator who already backed CLARITY
stories.summary: The crypto industry spent $55 million on a campaign defending a senator, even though that senator already supported the CLARITY Act, a crypto market-structure bill. The spending shows the industry's growing political war chest around the legislation.
stories.whyItMatters: Large political spending around market-structure legislation signals how much is riding on the bill's passage for the industry.
whatToWatch: Outcome of the race or campaign in question
Further crypto industry political spending disclosures
questions: Which senator and race does this involve?
Why defend a senator who already backed the bill?

stories.title: North Korea denies role in $6 billion Binance hack after FBI accusation
stories.summary: North Korea denied involvement in a $6 billion hack of Binance after the FBI publicly accused the country of carrying out the attack.
stories.whyItMatters: State-sponsored hacking accusations against a major exchange could bring sanctions or law enforcement action that affects the wider market.
whatToWatch: Further statements or action from the FBI or US government
Any sanctions tied to the accusation
Recovery of stolen funds, including those tracked in related Tether and Binance reports
questions: What evidence supports the FBI's accusation?
Will North Korea face new sanctions over the hack?
